name: Kang-Petrov Arms KP-19C 'Workhorse Compact'
description:
The KP-19C is the compact variant of the KP-19 'Workhorse' platform — same serialized lower frame architecture, same trigger group, same barrel-to-slide lockup geometry, but with the barrel trimmed to 88mm and the grip shortened to accommodate a 13-round flush-fit magazine. The result is a pistol that disappears under a jacket or into a sling bag with negligible printing, while accepting full-size KP-19 magazines with a visible grip extension. Dimensionally it is almost identical to a KP-19 when you fit the 17-round mag and extension — the compact designation refers to the default configuration, not the maximum. Chambered in 9x19mm Standard, with a factory option for 9x19mm Caseless conversion that requires a new barrel and breech face, sold as a Slagworks upgrade kit for Φ85.

The KP-19C occupies a particular niche between the full-size KP-17 and the micro-format pocket guns: it is the choice of people who need concealment but refuse to sacrifice shootability. Off-duty Tier 2 security contractors carry them. Courier workers who cross three ward boundaries a day and can't afford to look armed but absolutely need to be keep one clipped inside a cargo pocket. It's also the weapon of choice for the kind of person who has already been robbed once and decided it wouldn't happen again, which in GLMZ describes a significant demographic.

The compact frame develops a specific wear signature — the grip's shortened backstrap gets a groove worn into it by the middle finger, and the muzzle crown takes damage faster because owners who carry it loose in bags let it ride against zippers and fasteners for years. Most KP-19Cs in circulation have some degree of front-sight damage. It doesn't affect anything. The sights on these guns are considered vestigial by anyone who has used one in an actual confined-space encounter.
specifications: caliber: 9x19mm Standard effective_range: 40m rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic magazine_capacity: 13 rounds (flush) / 17 rounds (extended) weight: 0.64 kg
tactical_use: The KP-19C is a close-quarters concealed carry weapon for operators who prioritize discretion over capacity. The magazine interchangeability with the KP-19 platform means users who carry both — or work alongside partners who do — can share ammunition and magazines in a crisis. Tactically, operators run it with the flush 13-round magazine for concealment during approach and swap to an extended 17-round mag for sustained engagements. The shortened barrel costs roughly 10-15 meters of effective range compared to the full-size, which is irrelevant for the interior corridors and transit platforms where these guns most often get used.
cultural_context: The KP-19C is the concealment gun of the working class — not elegant, not aspirational, just practical. In neighborhoods where open carry marks you as a target for shakedowns by ACS patrols or rival groups, the ability to go undetected matters. The compact has a reputation among couriers and transit workers as the gun you bring when you can't bring a gun, which has made it mildly controversial — Arcturus Civil Security periodically runs confiscation sweeps in transit hubs and the KP-19C accounts for roughly 60% of civilian seizures. Most owners pay the fine and buy another one.
known_users: Tier 2 medical workers in low-security zones
story_hooks: An ACS seizure log shows 340 KP-19Cs confiscated from a single transit corridor over 90 days — the serial numbers, when traced, all link back to a single batch sold through a Slagworks company store that burned down the week after the sales were logged.

A courier is found dead in a freight elevator with her KP-19C still in her bag, fully loaded, safety off — she never drew it, which means whatever killed her she either didn't see coming or was told not to resist.
